task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 3, 2024. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: A magnitude 5.8 earthquake struck the Hollister Fault at 7:22 a.m. on September 3, 2024, with an epicenter 41 kilometers east of Harrington Bay.
The Western Seismic Alert Network issued an automated public warning 14 seconds before strong shaking reached Harrington Bay's downtown core.
The 14-second alert was triggered when WSAN's sensor station at Hollow Creek detected fault slip and calculated the wave travel time to the city.
It was the first time WSAN's system issued a live public warning during an actual damaging earthquake rather than a test.
The Harrington Bay Metro Authority halted three in-service trains and locked elevator banks at four underground stations in response to the alert.
No train derailments or elevator failures were reported; transit operations resumed within 32 minutes.
At least 47 people were treated at area hospitals for minor injuries, primarily cuts and bruises from falling objects.
WSAN director Dr. Lena Choi said: "Fourteen seconds is not a lot of time, but it is enough to stop a train, brace yourself, or step away from glass. Today showed that."
Metro Authority spokesman Tomás Reyes said dispatchers received the alert and triggered the emergency stop sequence before any controller heard the shaking.
The system sent alerts through cellphone emergency broadcast, a public siren network, and an integration with the metro's internal dispatch software.
Areas within 10 kilometers of the epicenter received no warning because shaking arrived before any signal could be transmitted — a known limitation of all current early warning systems.
WSAN's network comprises 187 seismic sensors installed between 2018 and 2022 at a total cost of $94 million.
Building damage was limited to cracked facades and broken windows in the downtown district; the Harrington Bay Office of Emergency Management reported no structural collapses.
The Hollister Fault last produced a damaging earthquake in 1978, a magnitude 6.1 event that caused widespread damage before modern early warning technology existed.
Federal seismological officials said the alert's accuracy — within 0.2 magnitude units of the final assessment — validated the network's detection algorithm.
Public alerts were delivered to an estimated 1.4 million mobile phones; a survey response system logged 22,000 replies within two hours.
Engineers will review the automated train-stop response to assess whether the 32-minute resumption time can be shortened in lower-severity events.
Dr. Choi said the agency plans to expand the sensor network by 40 stations over the next two years using state funding already appropriated.
The earthquake was felt as far as 180 kilometers away but caused no reported injuries outside Harrington County.
California, Oregon, and Washington state operate similar systems; Harrington Bay's WSAN was modeled on those networks and became operational in 2022.

a statement that the fault ruptured completely
a description of sensor technology not in the notes
